findings.finding: `shared_plan_prefix(plan)` is proposed as a public helper in `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` but will have at most 2 call sites by construction (1 production: `_resolve_system` in passes.py; 1 test-only: the byte-identity assertion in `test_shared_prefix.py`), falling below the Rule-of-Three threshold for a named abstraction in the shared prompting library. The existing `_resolve_system` already centralises the equivalent logic (`_SHARED_PREAMBLE + prompts.strip_volatile_marker(system)`) and serves as the single choke-point for all 7+ pass types. A helper that is only invoked by one production call-site and a test is premature abstraction.
scenarios: The helper is added to the shared `prompts.py` module (alongside `resolve_prompt`, `split_volatile`, etc.) establishing a public API contract with a single internal consumer — any future caller must match the exact preamble+plan layout, coupling them to an abstraction that was built for one use.

If the preamble or layout evolves (e.g. the exhaustiveness directive is refined), callers of `shared_plan_prefix` and `_resolve_system` must both be updated consistently — the abstraction doesn't reduce this burden with only 1 production call-site.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the helper in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` as `_shared_plan_prefix(plan: str) -> str` (private, co-located with `_SHARED_PREAMBLE`), and have `_resolve_system` delegate to it. The test can then import `passes._shared_plan_prefix` for the byte-identity assertion. Promote to `prompts.py` only if/when a third independent production call-site emerges.
